domain: Constitutional Political Economy / Monetary Theory / Corporate & Property Law
topic_summary: A non-canonical working packet for a hypothetical 'Constitution 2.0' project decomposing money, credit, property, insurance, taxation, and bankruptcy into separable constitutional powers. The core structural claim is that issuance quantity, credit judgment, public allocation, private underwriting, and productive deployment must be held by distinct actors so that no single node achieves either unlimited ownership aggregation or unlimited issuance authority. The packet poses 36 unresolved 'boss questions' and explicitly frames itself as hypotheses awaiting stock-flow-consistent modeling (the 'Keen Test') and audit-transparency modeling (the 'Skolnick Test').

key_entities: Monetary Organ (recursively composed constitutional body governing issuance quantity, bank regulation, financial backstops)
Legislative Root (enacts tax law, appropriates budgets, authorizes org accounts)
Judicial Root (owns bankruptcy, claim priority, final property adjudication)
State Organ (external political/economic interface; distinguishes trading partners from barbarians)
Bounded Private Corporations (500-seat ownership cap, natural-person termination, no recursive corporate ownership)
Commercial Banks (bounded corporations that intermediate national currency into corporate credit, do not create base money)
International Settlement Layer (neutral, technically distinct from domestic currency, candidate Ergo/DBDC implementation)
key_tensions: Distributed collective financial will (capacity for mass action) vs. concentrated authority over issuance/capital (functional sovereignty)
Bounded ownership nodes vs. unbounded consociation as the mechanism for mass capital formation
Monetary elasticity (responsive money supply) vs. damped credit feedback (preventing endogenous boom-bust)
Public monetary capacity becoming private productive capital vs. government not choosing private borrowers (socialist-market hybrid boundary)
Legible juridical-actor transparency vs. citizen privacy (surveillance-avoidant tax/VAT design)
National monetary sovereignty vs. external settlement reality (currency value is market-determined, not government-controlled)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The persisting shared commitment is the Boss Fight question itself: 'How does a proposed future acquire present purchasing power?' — i.e., what legitimates the conversion of not-yet-existing productive capacity into a present claim on real resources. Every financial institution described (money, credit, insurance, taxation, bankruptcy) is a different answer to this one kernel question, and the packet's authority (C2 constitutional ratification) depends on which answer it commits to.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: No single interpreter is enthroned. The packet explicitly distributes interpretive authority across the Monetary Organ (quantity), Legislature (allocation), Judiciary (final property termination), and State Organ (external legitimacy) — this multiplicity of interpreters is itself a structural choice about how the kernel question should be answered, distinguishing it from systems where one sovereign interprets unilaterally.

readings.commitment: A proposed future acquires present purchasing power legitimately only when a constituted, recursively composed political body (the Monetary Organ) deliberately votes to authorize new money, treating monetary quantity as a judgment to be constitutionally governed rather than an automatic formula. Legitimacy derives from the visibility and constitution of the deciding body, not from any external anchor.
readings.expected_structural_delta: Money supply changes only via legislatively-supervised organ vote; commercial bank lending cannot expand the payment medium; this reading makes 'who voted and what was their interest' the central observable and legitimating question, and treats interested-judgment disclosure (§15) as the primary safeguard rather than any external constraint.

readings.commitment: A proposed future acquires present purchasing power the moment a lender extends credit against expected repayment — commercial banks legitimately create purchasing power endogenously through the loan-creates-deposit mechanism (the Steve Keen / MMT description of actually-existing banking), because the bank's assessment of the future's creditworthiness IS the legitimating act. This reading treats the packet's own architecture (§12-13) as a doctrinal REJECTION of the mechanism this reading holds legitimate — it does not view endogenous money creation as a bug to be re-engineered away but as the correct and unavoidable answer to the kernel question.
readings.expected_structural_delta: Money supply is endogenous to aggregate private credit demand and bank risk appetite; the beneficiary set includes whoever can secure bank credit, and the victim set includes those excluded from credit access and those exposed to boom-bust cycles; this reading would classify C2's Monetary Organ as an artificial damping mechanism suppressing a naturally occurring (and in this reading, legitimate) process.

readings.commitment: A proposed future only legitimately commands present resources to the extent the claim is ultimately answerable in real physical terms — issuance is legitimate exactly insofar as it can clear against actual productive capacity (energy, labor, materials, compute). Legitimacy is not a property of WHO decides but of whether the resulting claims are physically redeemable; a deliberative vote and an endogenous bank loan are equally illegitimate if they generate claims physical output cannot satisfy.
readings.authority_grounding: physicalist / hard-money-adjacent (though explicitly NOT the gold-peg position the packet rejects in §10 — this reading is broader: any commitment that grounds legitimacy in real-resource answerability rather than institutional process)
readings.expected_structural_delta: The relevant observable is not who voted or who lent, but whether the Keen-Test stock-flow model closes against a physical-capacity layer (§38); this reading would treat a procedurally impeccable Monetary Organ vote that outstrips productive capacity as illegitimate on its own terms, and would treat an unauthorized endogenous loan that successfully mobilizes real slack capacity as substantively legitimate despite procedural irregularity.

readings.commitment: A proposed future acquires present purchasing power when and only when other market participants voluntarily extend it credit at a price — legitimacy is discovered through decentralized exchange (interest rates, bond yields, exchange rates) rather than declared by any constituted body or vetted against any physical model ex ante. The exchange rate signal described in §36 as 'delivering information' is, on this reading, the primary legitimating mechanism for ALL claims, not merely a residual check on external accounts.
readings.expected_structural_delta: Legitimating observable is price (yield spread, exchange rate movement, default probability priced by market), discovered continuously and dispersedly, versus the other readings' single-point institutional or physical tests; this reading would treat the Monetary Organ's deliberative vote itself as a distortion of the discovery process it should instead be deferring to, and treats §36's 'depreciation is not failure' concession as evidence the packet is already half-committed to this reading.

axiom_contradictions.basis: The deliberative reading's axiom is that legitimate quantity determination must be constitutionally centralized and visible to prevent private balance-sheet interest from covertly setting national money supply; the endogenous reading's axiom is that legitimate quantity determination is properly dispersed among private lenders responding to demand. A framework cannot simultaneously hold that dispersed private credit judgment is the correct locus of monetary legitimacy AND that such dispersed judgment must be constitutionally suppressed as illegitimate concentration of undeclared authority — accepting one requires negating the other.

The physicalist reading holds that a claim's legitimacy is an objective fact about real resource answerability, verifiable in principle by ex ante modeling independent of what any market currently prices; the catallactic reading holds that no such independent verification is possible or meaningful — legitimacy IS whatever price discovery reveals, and there is no fact about 'true' physical backing standing apart from and correcting market judgment. A framework cannot hold both that markets can be substantively wrong about physical answerability (physicalist) and that market price is the exhaustive and only test of legitimacy with no external corrective (catallactic).

The deliberative reading's axiom is that monetary quantity is a matter for accountable collective judgment precisely BECAUSE unmanaged market/credit processes produce social costs (boom-bust, concentration) that only visible constituted authority can dampen; the catallactic reading's axiom is that no constituted body can out-perform or legitimately override the informational content of decentralized price discovery, and that attempts to do so necessarily substitute someone's interested judgment for genuine discovery. Accepting that constituted deliberation is the appropriate legitimating mechanism requires denying that market discovery is self-sufficient, and vice versa.

axes.human_readable: The Boss Fight Kernel — How a Proposed Future Acquires Present Purchasing Power
axes.structural_delta: Not a single structural delta but a contested kernel: four incompatible axiomatic answers to what legitimates converting a not-yet-existing future into a present claim on real resources.
axes.primary_observable: Which mechanism (organ vote, private lending, physical-model closure, or market price) is treated as the terminal legitimating test when the mechanisms disagree.
axes.selection_reason: Kernel axis — counts as one axis per budget rule; expands into 4 readings in generation_sequence. Highest centrality: every other axis in the packet (banking architecture, bankruptcy, insurance, tax) is downstream of which answer to this question is assumed.

axes.human_readable: Bounded Corporate Ownership vs. Arbitrary-Scale Capital Formation
axes.structural_delta: A 500-seat, natural-person-terminating ownership cap with prohibited recursive corporate ownership, paired with a claim that capital scale can be decoupled from ownership scale via debt, consociation, and bank intermediation.
axes.primary_observable: Whether real-world capital-intensive ventures (e.g., semiconductor fabs, orbital infrastructure) can in fact be financed through the enumerated debt/consociation instruments without informally reconstructing concentrated ownership control via covenant, board-control, or creditor-governance rights.
axes.selection_reason: Passes independence test: distinct observable (ownership topology and capital-raising outcomes) from the kernel's issuance-legitimacy question and from the liability-termination axis; the packet itself flags this as Boss Questions 34/35, a self-identified hard test of the whole architecture.

axes.human_readable: Liability Termination Visibility — 'Where Does Failure Finally Land?'
axes.structural_delta: The claim that limited liability, securitization, insurance/reinsurance chains, and bankruptcy discharge do not eliminate loss but relocate it, and that a constitutional system must make the final resting place of every failure traceable to a specific claimant rather than allowing it to diffuse into an unaccountable public backstop.
axes.primary_observable: Whether, for any given financial failure (bank collapse, corporate bankruptcy, insurer insolvency), an external auditor (the 'Skolnick test') can reconstruct which specific party ultimately bears the loss, versus the loss becoming untraceable through chained guarantees/backstops/reinsurance.
axes.selection_reason: Passes independence test: distinct observable (traceability of loss termination) from both the kernel's legitimacy question and the ownership-topology axis; explicitly load-bearing across §6, §24-27, §37, and Boss Question 36, making it a structurally necessary third node rather than a restatement of the other two.

axes.human_readable: Domestic Monetary Sovereignty vs. External Settlement Reality
axes.structural_delta: The claim that domestic currency issuance and international settlement must be architecturally separate layers, such that domestic monetary sovereignty (control over issuance) is preserved precisely because the republic explicitly disclaims control over the currency's external market value or foreign productive capacity.
axes.primary_observable: Whether, under stress (persistent current-account imbalance, external shock), the domestic issuance mechanism can be insulated from pressure to defend a peg or absorb external claims in ways that would compromise the issuance-legitimacy answer selected at the kernel, versus the external seam forcing convergence toward one reading (e.g., market-discovered-confidence) regardless of which reading domestic law formally adopts.
axes.selection_reason: Passes independence test: distinct primary observable (insulation of domestic issuance from external market pressure) not reducible to ownership topology or liability termination; §29-36 and Boss Questions 27-33 treat this as a genuinely separate design seam with its own political-authorization mechanism (legislative+judicial+State root).

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Insurance distributed across Monetary/Preparedness/Health organs by subject matter rather than unified financial-industry jurisdiction
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Type A overlap: largely a specific instance of liability_termination_visibility (which organ ultimately backstops which failure) rather than an independently structured axis; folded into that axis's generation as a sub-case rather than deferred for centrality reasons.

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Value-added taxation mechanism that avoids both vertical-integration bias and universal transaction surveillance
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Genuinely distinct technical-design problem (§21) but zero centrality within the packet's own graph — no other axis depends on its resolution, and it does not feed into the kernel or the three selected axes. Available as omega/future expansion.

deferred_axes.structural_delta: State organ's binary distinction between polities receiving protected institutional interface and those excluded from it
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Correlated with domestic_currency_vs_external_settlement_seam (Type B partial entanglement — both concern the external interface) but has a distinct beneficiary/victim structure (recognized vs. unrecognized foreign counterparties) worth flagging; deferred rather than split out because packet gives it less independent load-bearing weight than the settlement-seam question (fewer downstream Boss Questions reference it directly).

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Bank constituents voting on monetary conditions that affect their own balance sheets
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: This is the central mechanism by which the issuance_as_deliberative_judgment READING is itself vulnerable to capture — better generated as internal texture of that reading during kernel expansion than as a free-standing fifth axis; would collapse into restating the reading's own stress-test (§15) rather than adding a new observable.

omegas.description: Verified the four issuance readings do NOT collapse: each assigns a different terminal test for legitimacy (constituted vote / private credit assessment / physical-model closure / market price) and the pairwise axiom-contradiction test confirms no single coherent framework holds any two of the three most divergent readings simultaneously. The packet's own text (§12, explicitly addressing 'the response to Steve Keen') confirms it is aware it is choosing among live, mutually exclusive positions rather than describing an uncontested design space.

A possible fifth reading — 'issuance as intergenerational trust' (legitimacy grounded in obligations to future persons not yet able to consent, relevant to moonshot/infrastructure framing in §7) — was considered and rejected as a distinct reading because the packet does not develop a terminal-test observable for it that differs structurally from issuance_as_deliberative_judgment (both cash out as 'a constituted present body decides on behalf of an absent party'); flagged here rather than fabricated into the readings array.

Bankruptcy (§24-26) was evaluated as a possible second contested kernel — 'what makes a property reallocation upon failed promise legitimate' — with candidate readings (contractarian priority-ordering vs. rehabilitative/going-concern vs. distributive/social-cost-spreading). It was NOT elevated to kernel status in this pass because the packet subordinates it definitionally to the liability_termination_visibility axis ('bankruptcy is the judicial protocol for converting failed promises into final property allocations') rather than treating it as contested at the constitutional level — the packet takes a firm position (no debt-to-prohibited-equity conversion) rather than presenting bankruptcy's legitimating logic as unresolved. Flagged for a future pass if this proves under-specified.
